intro:
Use it to show what a total is made of when there are too many parts for a pie chart. Each tile is one part, and its area is its share of the whole.

People compare areas badly, so a treemap is for ranking and grouping at a glance. Exact values belong in the labels, the readout or a `Breakdown` table.

The tiles are sorted largest first and share one colour that fades with rank, because the area already says which is bigger.

parts.Header: The strip above the box: `title`, `value` and `caption`, with your own control on the trailing side. Pass the value yourself, from `onActiveIndexChange` if it should follow the chart.
parts.Tiles: The rectangles. One part rather than one per datum, because a tile's box depends on every tile before it in its row.
parts.Skeleton: The box undivided, with a highlight moving across it, drawn only while `status` is `loading`.
parts.Labels: Names and values on the tiles. A tile shows both on two lines, both on one line, its name alone, or nothing, depending on its room.
parts.Tooltip: The readout for the tile being read. This is how the tiles too small to label are read.
parts.Legend: A swatch and a name per tile, under the box. Pointing at one reads its tile, and pressing it pins the reading.
parts.Breakdown: A table of every tile with its exact value and share. Reading a row lights its tile. It sits beside the box from 448 pixels wide and under it below that.

examples.title: A table beside the tiles
examples.description: Add `Breakdown` to name every tile, including the ones too small to label. A chart can use it in place of `Tooltip`, whose readout covers part of the tiles.

examples.title: A long tail
examples.description: `maxTiles` keeps the largest few and gathers the rest into one tile. Dropping the tail would rescale what is left, so every tile would claim a larger share than it has. `otherLabel` names the gathered tile.

examples.title: Picking one out
examples.description: A tile with its own `color` is drawn at full strength while the rest keep the ramp. `activeIndex` drives the reading from outside. It counts tiles as laid out, largest first.

examples.title: Wide tiles that lead somewhere
examples.description: `tileAspect` lays the tiles out wider, which leaves room for a name across a short chart. `color` also takes any CSS colour, such as one a user picked for a category. `onSelect` fires on a click, a tap or Enter, and not on hover.

examples.title: Loading, then data
examples.description: Add `TreemapChart.Skeleton` and drive `status`. The box is one plain rectangle until the data arrives, because placeholder tiles would look like a real split.

examples.title: Changing data
examples.description: Give each datum an `id` and its tile moves to its new box when `data` changes. Without one, a tile is identified by its row. A `ref` on the chart has `replay()`, which plays the entrance again.

notes:
### Sizing

The chart fills its container's width and takes its height from `aspectRatio`, which applies to the box alone, so a header does not shrink it. The tiles draw in the browser after the box has been measured, and the space is reserved until then, so they are not in server-rendered HTML.

### Bundle size

The chart adds about 60 KB of gzipped JavaScript to a page that uses it. A page that does not import it pays nothing, including one that imports other components from the package root.

### Colour

`color` names a role in the theme or takes any CSS colour, on the chart for the ramp and on a datum for one tile. Labels are white or near-black depending on the tile under them, so they stay readable on any colour in both themes.

### Reading a tile

Hovering a tile reads it and dims the others. A click or a tap pins the reading, a second one on the same tile lets go of it, and Escape clears it. `onActiveIndexChange` fires when the tile changes, so it can drive a readout outside the chart, as the first example does. For a tile that opens something, use `onSelect`, which does not fire on hover.

### Keyboard

The box takes focus. The arrow keys move between tiles, Enter or Space pins the reading and fires `onSelect`, and Escape clears it. The rows of `Legend` and `Breakdown` are buttons.

### Screen readers

Each tile is given as text beside the drawing. `label` names the chart and `labelForTile` writes a tile, for values with a unit.

### Negative values

Negative and non-finite values are treated as zero, because an area cannot be less than none.

### Reduced motion

With reduced motion set, the tiles and labels appear in place, and the skeleton's highlight is not drawn.
propsNote: `TreemapChart`, `TreemapChart.Header`, `TreemapChart.Legend` and `TreemapChart.Breakdown` also take the props of the element they render, and a `className`. `TreemapChart.Labels` puts its `className` on the layer of labels, and `TreemapChart.Tooltip` puts its own on the readout. The other parts take only the props listed.
